GS.rationale: Goldman Sachs has genuinely strong fundamentals: Q1 2026 revenue +14.4% YoY, EPS +24.3% YoY, operating margin at 37.7% (highest in sample), ROE improving to 14.7%, and net margin expanding to 0.299. The franchise is elite (#1 global M&A by deal value, 36.4% market share) and the strategic re-centering toward recurring AWM fees is sound. The near-term catalyst is real — SpaceX IPO on decision date with ~$500M estimated underwriting fees, and M&A pipeline on pace to approach 2021 record levels per President Waldron. However, Pillar 2 (valuation) is a significant headwind: P/B at 2.60× is at the ceiling of its 1-year range (1.6–2.7×), P/E at 17.7× is near the top of 13.4–18.6×, and the equity risk premium is only ~125 bps over the 10Y Treasury. The stock has already re-rated +31.5% in one quarter, faster than the +24.3% EPS growth. Balance-sheet leverage has worsened (16.8× vs 14.2× YoY) as equity declined while assets grew 16.7%. The strong franchise and real near-term IPO/M&A catalysts prevent a negative score, but the stretched valuation relative to own history and rising leverage cap the upside. Score reflects a good business at a full price with a modest catalyst boost.
